name: 1X World Model
summary: 1X trained an action-conditioned video world model on data from its humanoid fleet, aimed less at generating training data than at evaluating policies. Because real-robot evaluation is slow, dangerous and non-reproducible, simulating candidate policies inside a learned model of the robot's own environment gives a fast comparison signal. The team released data and ran a public challenge around the model.
innovation: Framed world models primarily as an evaluation instrument for robot policies.
Trained on proprietary humanoid interaction data rather than generic internet video.
matters: Addresses evaluation, arguably the field's worst bottleneck, from an unusual angle.
limits: A learned evaluator inherits its own model bias; agreement with real-world ranking is unproven.
lineage: Genie-style action-conditioned video models applied to humanoid policy evaluation.
